question: to the Commission Kosma Złotowski (ECR) Subject:

The disruption in the Strait of Hormuz has caused major shocks to global oil supplies. The International Energy Agency warns that the European Union has sufficient aviation fuel reserves for about six weeks and that there may be systemic shortages of aviation fuel in the near future. Member States, as well as the European Union itself, are therefore calling on individuals and businesses to save fuel and reduce travel. Airlines are already cancelling flights and grounding part of their fleets. Lufthansa has announced that it is cutting 20 000 short-haul flights over the summer on account of the sharp increase in fuel prices and the drop in profitability of many routes. Other airlines are also temporarily reducing connections or increasing ticket prices, passing on the rising costs to passengers. In light of the above: 1.

Is the Commission analysing how Regulation (EU) 2023/2405 and its implications are affecting the current crisis situation, in particular the availability and price of aviation fuel and, more broadly, the cost of airfares?

Is the Commission considering introducing flexibility mechanisms under Regulation (EU) 2023/2405, e.g. through implementing and delegated acts, enabling the suspension or adjustment of mandatory SAF blending levels in the event of serious disruptions in the fuel market?

In the event of a prolonged crisis in the availability of fuels, including aviation fuel, is the Commission considering proposing a reform of the ReFuelEU Aviation Regulation and, if so, what direction might such a reform take?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.6.2026) 1. The Regulation (EU) 2023/2405 (ReFuelEU Aviation)1 aims to scale-up Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and ensure that SAF is widely available and affordable in the EU. It creates a predictable framework for producing and using SAF, while strengthening the EU’s energy resilience and reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels. As announced in AccelerateEU2, the Commission is establishing a Fuel Observatory to improve visibility over fuel supply and demand, help detect shortages, and support targeted action such as alternative sourcing or coordinated stock releases in the EU. 2. As announced in AccelerateEU, the Commission issued on 8 May 2026 guidance3 on the flexibilities available under EU aviation legislation to ensure a coordinated response across Member States. Specifically, on ReFuelEU Aviation, the guidance clarifies how airlines can be exempted from their refuelling obligation in case of fuel shortage. The crisis in the Middle East reinforces the need to accelerate the transition towards more diversified energy sources. Maintaining the ambition of ReFuelEU Aviation and implementing the Sustainable Transport Investment Plan (STIP)4 are therefore essential to strengthen Europe’s energy security, strategic autonomy and competitiveness. 3. As announced in AccelerateEU, if the situation worsens and existing flexibilities no longer suffice, the Commission will propose temporary changes to the applicable EU legislative framework, where justified.
